shot.caption: The web interface every pool serves, here with demo figures at mainnet scale.

modes.heading: Solo for yourself. Shared for everyone else
modes.subtitle: One setting decides who gets paid. Start solo; switch when other miners join.

direct.title: Solo mining
direct.description: The node mines straight to your address, so every block reward lands in your wallet. The pool tracks your rigs, shares and blocks, and never sends a transaction.

facts.label: Rewards
facts.value: Paid by the chain to your address

facts.label: Good for
facts.value: Your own rigs, behind one address

pool.title: Shared pool
pool.description: Rewards land at the pool's address and are split between miners by their shares, minus your fee, then paid out by the node as ordinary transactions.

facts.label: Payout schemes
facts.value: PPLNS by default, PPLNSBF, PROP or SOLO

facts.label: Payouts
facts.value: From 1 LAX, every 10 minutes by default

facts.label: Keys on the server
facts.value: The pool's own key, unlocked in the node

start.heading: Mining in minutes
start.subtitle: Everything runs in Docker. Two values in a .env file are all it needs.

steps.title: Set two values
steps.description: Copy .env.example to .env and set POOL_ADDRESS, your LAX address, and a database password.

steps.title: Start it
steps.description: docker compose up -d starts the node, PostgreSQL and the pool. The pool waits for the node to sync, then opens stratum on port 4073.

steps.title: Point your rigs at it
steps.description: Miners use their LAX address as the user name. The web interface on port 4000 builds the command for them.

solo.label: Solo
solo.note: Set POOL_ADDRESS and DB_PASSWORD in .env before starting. Solo is the default: rewards go straight to POOL_ADDRESS and the server holds no keys.

shared.label: Shared pool
shared.note: Creates a password and a pool account in the node's volume. Set POOL_ADDRESS to the new address, PAYOUT_MODE=pool, and NODE_EXTRA_ARGS to unlock it (the README has the line), then start. Back up the keystore and the password: together they control the pool's funds.

miners.label: Connect a rig
miners.note: Any XHash miner that speaks EthereumStratum works. Use d=0.5 as the stratum password for a fixed share difficulty.

features.heading: A full pool, built for Parallax
features.subtitle: A Parallax-only fork of Miningcore, the open-source pool engine. Its stratum server, share accounting and payout engine, with XHash and Parallax's rules built in.

xhash.title: XHash validation
xhash.description: Every share is hashed by the pool itself, in native code, from a light cache of a few megabytes per epoch.

stratum.title: EthereumStratum
stratum.description: The stratum Hashwarp and SRBMiner-Multi speak, with legacy eth-proxy and TLS ports available from a config file.

vardiff.title: Adaptive difficulty
vardiff.description: Each miner's share difficulty follows its hashrate, aiming for a share every 15 seconds. Miners can also fix their own.

maturity.title: Parallax's maturity rule
maturity.description: Rewards are credited only after the 100-block lockbox, about 17 hours, from the halving schedule the chain itself uses.

ui.title: A web interface
ui.description: Pool hashrate, expected time to a block, recent blocks, payments, a page per miner, and a connect page that builds the miner command.

api.title: REST API and live events
api.description: Pools, blocks, payments and miners over REST, and a WebSocket stream for new blocks, unlocks, payments and hashrate.

zeroConfig.title: No setup to speak of
zeroConfig.description: Configured from environment variables alone. It creates its own database schema on first start.

ops.title: Operator tools
ops.description: Prometheus metrics, banning, e-mail and Pushover alerts, and ZeroMQ share relays for pools spread over several servers.

operators.heading: Before you open it to others
operators.subtitle: A shared pool holds other people's earnings in a hot wallet. A few things matter more than the rest.

rpc.title: Keep the node's RPC private
rpc.description: In pool mode the node holds the unlocked pool key: anyone who reaches its RPC can spend from it. Compose keeps the RPC inside the project; keep it that way.

keys.title: Back up the key and the password
keys.description: The keystore and its password sit in the node's volume. Together they control the pool's funds. Lose them and the funds are gone.

admin.title: Admin and metrics stay local
admin.description: The admin API and /metrics answer only to the machine the pool runs on. Mind that behind a reverse proxy on the same host, every visitor looks local.

config.title: Outgrow the .env with a config file
config.description: TLS stratum, several ports, notifications, share relays and multiple pools are set in a JSON config file. Every option is in the schema.
